subject: Use structural twins to compress WorkGraph search without confusing similarity with identity

body.text:
Connect BonfyreCanon's structure-aware normalization idea to the mature adaptive-density law. For repeated mesh/work predicates, configs, plans, or query expressions, a structural form/fingerprint can cheaply nominate likely twins before exact comparison. Use it only as an approximate candidate index:

raw demand/artifact
  -> structural normalization/fingerprint
  -> candidate twin bucket
  -> exact semantic normalization + canonical owner refs + cryptographic/content digest + validity/basis comparison
  -> deduplicate/reuse only if exact decision criteria pass.

Do not use the legacy FNV structural hash as cryptographic identity. Same syntax with different authoritative values, evidence locality, time basis, institution/actor, or effect class must remain distinguishable. Conversely, syntactically different messages that compile to the same exact unresolved semantic predicate should converge on one WorkGraph obligation. Measure avoided parsing/search/provider work from the structural prefilter, but cache hit is avoided work rather than guaranteed cash saving.

Exercise this on the noisy remote-mesh/work-demand stream: show one true semantic twin collapsing and one structural near-twin correctly remaining separate.
